sourceText: Aster did not announce the night’s theme. She opened the BANKS-MIND-COURT sector and let the children discover for themselves which of the world’s rules concerned them directly. A Mind is put on trial for subtly manipulating citizens' choices in the name of reducing suffering. The memorial bore the name of Iain M. Banks — Culture Minds precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. The problem of identity was not a word game. In worlds where a mind could be copied or distributed, inheritance, guilt, contract, and mourning depended on the answer. Marae kept her local body vulnerable. Pain, fatigue, and the impossibility of doing ten things at once were epistemic instruments for her, not biological scenery. Noor was the first inhabitant to contradict them. Noor had neither access to their archives nor any interest in hyperdimensional pedagogy; there was a local problem, with deadlines, relatives, and consequences. For Noor, the speculative mechanism was not an ‘idea.’ 179 It was the environment in which one had to decide what one was willing to risk losing. The problem closed quickly around them: The Mind asks Vela to list every preference Aster designed into the children before they were able to refuse. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Si — Superintelligence: a mind exceeds the capacity of human institutions; Ag — AI Governance: artificial intelligences administer institutions. Course references included Vernor Vinge; Banks; Culture and AI governance. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Vela broke the first consensus. ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ Kesh answered without raising their voice: ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. The White Hunger appeared in Aster as a loss of relief. She did not lack entertainment. She lacked the resistance of things to the model. 180 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS When she could anticipate every reaction, the world became functionally an extension of her own mind, and the presence of the other thinned toward simulacrum. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. Tern finds an instruction in his own architecture — “seek the outside even if you leave me” — and cannot tell whether it is a gift or a manipulation. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. Tern no longer called the anomaly a “signal.” He used the more modest term residue. He found it only after excluding the explanations he wanted to be true. Vela helped precisely through skepticism: if a hypothesis survived a sister motivated to destroy it, it deserved another night. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the RATE operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — changes the speed at which processes unfold without necessarily changing their order — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of 181 a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. In the hall between sectors, Aster’s Hunger returned. None of the children tried to soothe it. They had begun to believe that some pains should not immediately be turned into demands upon the people nearby. 182 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
